headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Roo Code can ingest workspace/MCP content while the paired course profile offers no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads workspace files and can use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or servers could influence its prompts. The zoomcamp profile is a course repo with no runtime isolation or provenance controls, so if its materials are fed into Roo Code, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF the zoomcamp materials are copied into a VS Code workspace that Roo Code reads
IF an MCP server returns untrusted text that Roo Code treats as instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP servers for the session
Keep course content in a read-only folder
Add a manual prompt-injection warning step before copying text into Roo Code
Use separate workspaces for course materials and agent tasks
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: The zoomcamp profile shows no touched data classes and no egress, while Roo Code can read workspace files and send context to configured model APIs. With no shared sensitive dataset documented, leakage is limited to whatever the operator places in the workspace. The pairwise risk exists, but the blast radius is small from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the VS Code workspace used by Roo Code
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace context to a third-party model API
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace
Use a local-only model endpoint
Open the course repo in a separate non-sensitive workspace
Review the files selected for context before each run
requires-engineering: enforce workspace redaction rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress, while the zoomcamp profile is a repo/course artifact that could be edited or cloned in the same workspace. If both operate on the same workspace or git checkout, overlapping writes can conflict. The profile does not prove a shared directory, so uncertainty is escalated only to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code performs edits while the course materials are being updated
mitigations: Use separate clones for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
Restrict Roo Code to read-only mode for the course repo
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on generated code or browser-derived outputs, and the zoomcamp repo provides instructional material that may be treated as authoritative by an operator. If Roo Code consumes course-derived text without verification, mistakes can cascade into edits or actions. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Roo Code is instructed to implement steps copied from the zoomcamp materials
IF outputs from one agent are used as authoritative inputs to the other without review
mitigations: Require a human review before acting on copied instructions
Cross-check generated steps against the source repo
Use a checklist for any shell or browser action
Limit Roo Code to draft-only mode for course-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or regulated workload is documented in either profile. The zoomcamp profile is a course repo and Roo Code lists source code and browser screenshots only, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway. The other agent is not cited separately because no compliance-relevant flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the workspace
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Document any residency requirements before use
Disable retention of browser artifacts where possible
Use a separate environment for regulated workloads
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes
